title: Book One · Chapter 3: Dad’s Hands
story:
In the morning, Ronan wakes up on the floor.

His blanket is warm, but the floor is hard.

Where is his bed? He looks around the room.

Then he sees it by the door. Dad took it apart for the move. The long pieces stand against the wall.

Today they move to the new home.

Ronan sits up.

Mum is putting bowls in a bag. She puts a towel between them.

“Why?” Ronan asks.

“The towel keeps them apart. Then they don’t hit each other.”

“Do bowls fight?”

“Only in bags.”

Ronan looks inside. There are three bowls. They all look quiet.

Outside, Dad is loading a cart. The cart has two wheels and long handles. It belongs to Dad's friend. Dad can use it this morning.

Ronan carries his small box to the door.

Dad takes it and puts it beside the bag of clothes. He puts the pieces of the bed down one side. Mum brings out the blankets.

“Can I hold the cart?” Ronan asks.

“Stand here,” Dad says. “Keep both hands on this part.”

Ronan holds it very tightly.

Dad lifts a bag onto the cart.

The handle of the bag breaks.

One end falls. A blue shirt drops onto the road.

Mum picks it up.

Dad looks at the broken handle. Then he looks at the bag. He presses his lips together.

“I can carry that one,” Mum says.

“You have two bags already.”

Dad puts it down.

Ronan holds the cart. His arms begin to hurt a little.

“Dad?”

Dad turns at once.

“You can let go now. Thank you.”

Ronan opens his hands. There are red marks across them.

Dad gets his blue box.

He takes out a short piece of rope. He puts it through the two sides of the old handle.

“Can you hold this end?”

Ronan takes it.

“Like this?”

“Yes. Keep it there.”

Dad pushes the rope through the handle again. His fingers move quickly. Ronan can see the little cut on one of them.

“Does it hurt?”

“A little.”

“Then stop.”

Dad looks at him.

“One more bit,” he says. “Then I can stop.”

He pulls the rope tight. He lifts the bag a little, puts it down, and checks the handle. Then he lifts it higher.

The new handle holds.

“Now you try,” he says.

Ronan lifts one end. Dad holds the other.

Together, they put the bag on the cart.

Ronan looks at Dad’s blue box.

“That box is very heavy.”

“It is.”

“But we need it.”

“Yes. We need those tools.”

Mum comes out with the last bag. She looks through the door once more. Then she closes it.

Dad stands between the long handles. He lifts them slowly.

The cart moves.

Ronan walks beside it. He can see the corner of his box under a blanket.

“I helped with that bag,” he tells Mum.

“I saw.”

At the end of the street, Dad stops to rest.

Ronan stands beside him. He puts his small hand next to Dad’s large one on the handle.

He does not push.

He just leaves it there.
studyGuide:
## 先看情节提示也可以

搬家时袋子提手断了；爸爸用绳子修好，Ronan帮忙握住绳头。

## 从认词到读句子

1. **Dad / gets / his blue box.** 爸爸／拿来／他的蓝色工具箱。
2. **Ronan / holds / the cart.** Ronan／握住／搬家车。

---

## 重点词句

| 表达 | 本章意思 |
|---|---|
| lift | 抬起、提起 |
| handle | 提手、把手 |
| rope | 绳子 |
| let go | 松手 |

旧词复现：hold、keep、bag、box、hand、tool、put … down、check。

辅助理解：cart＝搬东西用的车；wheel＝轮子；towel＝毛巾。

“The new handle holds.”这里的 holds 表示“撑得住、没有断”，比前面“用手握住”的意思有所扩展。

## 理解与回访

1. 搬家过程中，哪个东西出了问题？Dad 怎样处理？
2. Ronan 实际帮了什么忙？

换个场景看旧词：*Check the box before you send it.* check 是“检查”，将来也会在发货场景中出现。
